newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude slightly lower, MidEast trades steady.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude slightly lower, MidEast trades steady.

text.p: Asian crude prices were slightly lower on Monday with Middle East grades trading around flat, while regional grades were on hold pending the release of the Indonesian allocations.
Futures prices continued to find support after the short covering rally last week and the firmer tone to Brent supported the Brent/Dubai differentials in the face of steady Dubai.
May Brent/Dubai was assessed at $1.50/$1.57 per barrel, after a U.S. refiner sold the spread at $1.57 to a European major late on Friday.
That compared with $1.40/$1.50 in late New York Friday.

In Middle East trading, a Japanese trader was heard selling a cargo of Umm Shaif to a U.S. major at ADNOC plus one cent, while a European major was heard paying ADNOC flat to a Malaysian trader for a cargo of Murban.
Traders said the prices were in line with expectations for the May trading market. Last week Oman traded between plus two and flat.
Traders said two Dubai cargoes for May were traded at 28.5 cents over full-month quotes. Both cargoes went to a U.S. major.
The regional market was quiet as it waited for the April export allocations by Pertamina.
Trading sources said Pertamina allocated 61,000 bpd of Minas for April, down from 94,300 in March.
March was a relatively high allocation because of the 38-day turnaround of the 120,000 bpd Dumai refinery and the unexpected shut down of the 125,000 bpd Balongan refinery.
However, traders said they still expected a million barrels of Minas to overhang the market in April, but that official allocations would be kept normal to support the market.
April allocations of Duri were 70,700 bpd, up from 45,700 a month earlier. Traders said the higher allocation reflected the overhang of Duri, also owing to the refinery problems.
